## Two Changes to Selective Availability

Selective Availability deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. The U.S. government addressed the feature in two separate steps: first, it stopped using it; later, it specified that it would not be included in a future generation of GPS.

At President Bill Clinton’s direction, the government stopped using Selective Availability in May 2000 to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide. In September 2007, it announced that the future GPS III generation would be procured without the feature.

The 2007 announcement did not mark the operational change—that had occurred in 2000. Instead, omitting Selective Availability from GPS III made the 2000 policy durable for that generation.
